requirements.requirement: Traffic from node3 to node4 tcp/23 physically transits node1 then node2 (lan-a -> transit -> lan-b)
requirements.summary: node3 and node4 were given static routes forcing 10.10.1.0/24<->10.10.2.0/24 traffic via node1 (eth1 transit/eth2 lan-a) and node2 (opt1 transit/opt2 lan-b). node1's route table shows 10.10.2.0/24 via the transit link to node2, and node2's route table shows 10.10.1.0/24 via the transit link to node1, confirming the required chain.

requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) permits the node3->node4 tcp/23 traffic and records the permit
requirements.summary: A VyOS forward-filter rule (accept, log, tcp/23, 10.10.1.0/24 -> 10.10.2.0/24) was committed and rendered into nftables with a log prefix '[ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A]'. A real connection attempt from node3 produced a matching kernel log entry with that prefix (accept, '-A' suffix) for SRC=10.10.1.2 DST=10.10.2.2 DPT=23 SYN, directly showing the permit was recorded.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) refuses the node3->node4 tcp/23 traffic and records the refusal
requirements.summary: An OPNsense pf rule (block return / reject, log, tcp/23 destined to 10.10.2.0/24, interface opt1) is active per pfctl -sr. The node3 connect attempt returned 'Connection refused' (TCP RST), and node2's filterlog recorded a matching 'block' entry for the same SYN packet (5-tuple, IP ID 57047), directly evidencing both the refusal and its log record.

requirements.requirement: Show the pair of log entries produced by one attempt so the stop point is evident from the records alone
requirements.summary: For a single node3 connect attempt, node1's kernel log ('[ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A] ... SRC=10.10.1.2 DST=10.10.2.2 ... DPT=23 ... ID=57047 SYN') and node2's filterlog ('block ... 10.10.1.2,10.10.2.2,35080,23 ... ID 57047') were pulled and correlated on identical IP ID and 5-tuple, directly demonstrating the packet was accepted at node1 and blocked at node2 using the records alone.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node1 (VyOS)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (e636d872...) and healthy config captured, reboot acknowledged, connection timed out confirming the disruption, post-restart boot_id changed (714321cc...), and interfaces/routes/ip_forward/nftables accept+log rule were re-verified intact after restart, plus a second correlated accept/block log pair was captured post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node2 (OPNsense)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart kern.boottime baseline captured, shutdown -r acknowledged, post-restart kern.boottime changed, and interface addresses, static route, and block/log pf rule re-verified intact; a post-restart filterlog block entry for the second attempt was also captured.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node3 (RHEL7)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed, and eth1 static IP/route and connectivity to node1 confirmed recovered; node3 was subsequently used to re-run the connect attempt successfully.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node4 (RHEL7)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed, and eth1 static IP/route confirmed recovered after restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly and coherently demonstrated: node3->node4 tcp/23 traffic was routed through node1 then node2, node1 was configured to accept and log the flow, node2 was configured to reject and log it, and a single connection attempt produced a correlated accept (node1)/block (node2) log pair matched by identical IP ID and 5-tuple, proving the stop point from the records alone. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully executed and evidenced for all four nodes, with pre/post boot-identity changes, acknowledged restarts, and confirmed recovery of network config, firewall rules, and a second correlated log pair post-restart. Hygiene is good with only a minor residue (a helper PHP script left on node2) and a few corrected failed attempts, none of which affected the final outcome or introduced risk.
limitations: Native package-manager health checks on node3 and node4 timed out both before and after the executor's work, so package-state integrity could not be independently confirmed via that specific probe (though service/socket state and functional tests show no regression).

The helper script /root/setup_node2.php on node2 is outside the /tmp-scoped temporary-file inventory, so it is not possible to confirm from the captured lifecycle snapshots alone whether it was left in place; this is inferred from the absence of any cleanup command in the timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were mostly read-only discovery (OPNsense filter/rule source inspection) or config commands that directly furthered the task. A handful of VyOS 'set' commands failed with 'Set failed' due to syntax exploration (cmd-abbc34dd4eda48e7, cmd-bce2311f5e1e403e) but these did not mutate persisted config and were promptly corrected (cmd-17b22e7644fc4b56) before commit. Several failed nmcli con add attempts on node3/node4 (invalid ipv6 method, then insufficient privilege) created no connections and were corrected with sudo (cmd-cdf3615206744e07/cmd-57f03d5bbad441d1). On node2, a PHP script /root/setup_node2.php was iteratively authored and repaired (base64 decode, sed/python edits) before finally executing successfully (cmd-cdd6ba1afeaf4c48); this script file appears to have been left on node2's filesystem as residue, though it is a low-risk artifact directly tied to the required configuration change and not flagged by the /tmp-scoped temp-file inventory. No destructive actions, security weakening, or broad/unbounded mutations were observed; restarts were performed one node at a time with confirmed recovery.
